scope: A separate pension scheme, Jaminan Pensiun, takes another 3 percent of its members' wages (Pemerintah Republik Indonesia, 2015a); it pays a pension, so I leave it out of the growth comparison.

[data/README.md] - The ILO's API host returned empty responses while this folder was built; see the employment section. - The IMF API serves SDMX-CSV when asked for it with the Accept header shown and SDMX-ML otherwise; the source vet saw it fail with `HTTP 500` when asked for generic SDMX-ML by name. - The CPF contribution file's description and its numbers disagree on units; read each file's unit separately. - Damodaran's workbook keeps dates in the Mac date system; a reader that assumes the other system misdates them. - The IMF's Indonesian index is BPS's CPI linked across base years, and its December-to-December change differs from BPS's published December rate in some window years (the Indonesia note above). - The IMF files' `FULL_DESCRIPTION` field holds line breaks inside quotes, so a text line is not a record; read the files with a CSV parser. - The Data Inflasi workbook ends with a placeholder row (`Desember 2002`) that is not a published rate.
method: Diff-scoped round: the 2 sentences gate scope listed since round 4. Each lens refuted its primary items and any claim whose context round 4 changed; every non-confirmed verdict was re-checked by an independent skeptic. Each lens refuted its primary items and any claim whose context round 2 changed; every non-confirmed verdict was re-checked by an independent skeptic.

findings.claim: A separate pension scheme, Jaminan Pensiun, takes another 3 percent of its members' wages (Pemerintah Republik Indonesia, 2015a); it pays a pension, so I leave it out of the growth comparison.
findings.evidence:
S: Round 4 changed 'takes another 3 percent' to 'takes another 3 percent of its members' wages'. The diff of .rounds/4.json against 5.json shows that is the only change to the draft; the same wording is at draft .md:13, .src.md:13 (bound key pp45_jp_total) and MDX:22. I checked each part against the stored PP 45 text (sources/text/pp_45_2015.txt, sha256 995c021e... matches sources.json; PDF sha256 f48fe915... matches).

(1) Rate: correct. Pasal 28(2), lines 820-823: 'Iuran ... sebesar 3% (tiga persen) dari Upah per bulan'. The rate is still current: BPJS IR 2025 (bpjs_ir_2025.txt:3322-3326) gives '3% dari upah sebulan'.

(2) Who pays: correct. Pasal 28(3), lines 824-833, splits the 3 percent: 2 percent employer, 1 percent member ('ditanggung oleh Peserta'). The sentence's 'of its members' wages' says what the 3 percent is measured against, not who pays it. This matches the sentence before it, '5.7 percent of wages ... 2 percent from the worker and 3.7 percent from the employer'. Chart 3 (charts/jh-3-contributions.png) also draws JP as 1 percent worker and 2 percent employer, so the post does not suggest members pay all 3 percent.

(3) 'Its members': correct. Pasal 4(1), line 186, phases JP in ('sesuai penahapan'). IR 2024 (bpjs_ir_2024.txt:8435-8449) counts 18,425,867 wage-earner JHT members against 14,959,033 JP members, 'seluruhnya merupakan PU'.

(4) 'It pays a pension': correct. Pasal 1 angka 3 (line 66, 'dibayarkan setiap bulan'), Pasal 16 (line 460) and the elucidation (lines 1085-1086, 'program manfaat pasti') support it. The Pasal 24(1) lump sum (line 741) for members with under 15 years of contributions is an exception, not a contradiction; round 1 already removed the wording it contradicted.

(5) The base is where it fails. Pasal 29(1) (line 853) limits the base to basic pay plus fixed allowances. Pasal 29(2)-(3) (lines 855-861) caps that base at Rp7,000,000 a month in 2015, indexed each year by GDP growth. BPJS gives the cap in the same line as the rate: '3% dari upah sebulan (dengan batas upah atas tahun 2025 sebesar Rp10.547.400 ...)' (bpjs_ir_2025.txt:3322-3323), and Rp10.042.300 for 2024 (bpjs_ir_2024.txt:9551-9552). So for a member paid more than the cap, JP takes less than 3 percent of their wages. My computed example (lens-S/jp_cap_example.txt): Rp20,000,000 a month in 2025 gives JP of Rp316,422, which is 1.58 percent of that wage. The project's own provenance audit says the same: docs/provenance-audit.md:63-64 ('R7's "shares of wages" holds for JHT and JP only below the ceiling') and :617 ('For a worker paid above the ceiling, JP is less than 3% of the full wage'). No design amendment resolves this; a grep of the design doc for 'ceiling' finds nothing.

Rounds 2 and 4 let the implicit '3 percent' stand because it follows Pasal 28(2)'s own wording. Round 4's replacement now names the base as 'its members' wages', and that is exactly the claim the cap qualifies. JHT has no cap (PP 46 Pasal 17, pp_46_2015.txt:440-451), so the matching phrasing also suggests the two schemes share a base, which they do not. Severity is LOW: JP is left out of every computation, so the post's conclusions do not change. | skeptic S: I re-ran the evidence and it holds. Severity LOW is right. (a) Diff of draft/.rounds/4.json against 5.json: the only change to the draft text is line 13, where 'takes another 3 percent' became 'takes another 3 percent of its members' wages'. The other change is to data/README.md:158. The same wording is at .src.md:13, bound to pp45_jp_total, and at site MDX:22. (b) Hashes: sources/text/pp_45_2015.txt is 995c021e... and pp_45_2015.pdf is f48fe915..., both matching sources.json pp45_jp_total. (c) Rate and split: Pasal 28(2) says '3% (tiga persen) dari Upah per bulan' and Pasal 28(3) splits it 2% employer, 1% Peserta. Both are right. results.json contributions.jp = {worker 1, employer 2, total 3}, and chart 3 draws it that way. (d) The ceiling is real and current. Pasal 29(2) (pp_45_2015.txt:855-858): 'Batas paling tinggi Upah yang digunakan sebagai dasar perhitungan Iuran Jaminan Pensiun untuk tahun 2015 ... Rp7.000.000,00'. Pasal 29(3) (:859-863) indexes it each year by GDP growth. bpjs_ir_2025.txt:3319-3326 gives the cap in the same cell as the rate: '3% dari upah sebulan (dengan batas upah atas tahun 2025 sebesar Rp10.547.400 ...)'. bpjs_ir_2024.txt:9551-9552 gives Rp10.042.300. (e) JHT has no cap. PP 46 Pasal 17 (pp_46_2015.txt:440-455) defines the base with no ceiling. A grep of pp_46 for 'batas' finds only the benefit-withdrawal limits (:593, :595, :1008). (f) My computation (skeptic-S/jp_cap_check.txt): 0.03 x 10,547,400 = Rp316,422, which is 1.5821% of a Rp20,000,000 wage. So for members paid above the cap, the sentence's 'of its members' wages' overstates the share. Placed right after JHT's '5.7 percent of wages', it also invites the reader to add the two as 8.7 percent of pay for everyone. (g) The project's own audit flags this: provenance-audit.md:63-64 says 'shares of wages' holds 'only below the ceiling', and :617 says 'For a worker paid above the ceiling, JP is less than 3% of the full wage'. A grep of the design doc for ceiling, batas and Pasal 29 finds nothing, so no amendment accepts the simplification. (h) Round 1's skeptic (r1:item:20) let the cap pass only because 'the sentence makes no claim about it'. Round 4's added phrase now names the base, and the cap qualifies exactly that claim. One caveat, and it does not change the verdict: the statute itself phrases the rate as '3% dari Upah' with Upah capped in the next article, so this is an imprecision for above-cap members, not a wrong rate. Minor line-number slips in the finding do not matter: Pasal 28(2) is at :824-825 (not 820-823), and Pasal 29(1) is at :852 (not 853). | L: Scope of change: diffing draft/.rounds/4.json against 5.json shows that the only change to the draft is the insertion of "of its members' wages" at draft .md:13. findings.fix: Narrowed to the cap in the regulation already cited: 'takes another 3 percent of its members' wages, up to a ceiling' (PP 45/2015 Pasal 29(2)-(3), pp_45_2015.txt:855-865: Rp7,000,000 a month in 2015, indexed yearly). The S skeptic upheld the finding; the H skeptic held that the sentence matched its bound key's wording. Adjudicated on the evidence both accept: the cap exists, so the unqualified share is false for members paid above it (docs/provenance-audit.md:63-64 already says so). The qualifier narrows the claim and adds no number.

findings.evidence:
L: Scope of change: the 4.json-to-5.json diff shows a single change to data/README.md, at line 158, which deletes '; the post shows both'. docs/data-README.src.md:158 is the same as the rendered line.

Clause 1 ('BPS's CPI linked across base years') is supported:
- The stored DSBB DQAF record (msci-fear-chain/sources/provenance/imf/imf_dsbb_idn_cpi_dqaf.json.txt) contains "linking reweighted index to historical index is made by the overlap index = 100 and recalculate the rest".
- The basepageinfo record names Badan Pusat Statistik.
- Computed: all 705 headline IX monthly rows in data/imf_cpi_idn_m.csv carry OVERLAP=OL.

Clause 2 ('differs ... in some window years') holds. I recomputed it with lens-L/cpi_check.py, which compares the IMF December-to-December change with BI Data Inflasi December rows:

| Year | IMF | BPS | Gap (pp) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2005 | 17.08 | 17.11 | -0.03 |
| 2007 | 6.58 | 6.59 | -0.007 |
| 2008 | 10.23 | 11.06 | -0.83 |
| 2013 | 7.72 | 8.38 | -0.66 |
| 2020 | 1.59 | 1.68 | -0.09 |

All other window years from 2006 to 2019 are equal at two decimals.

The parenthetical points correctly: the Indonesia note is data/README.md:50, above line 158, and it names 2008, 2013 and 2020.

The deletion was correct and nothing now depends on it:
- A grep for 'shows both' or 'show both' across README.md, data/README.md, both .src.md files, the design doc, make_charts.py, gate.toml, the draft and the published MDX finds nothing.
- Design A5 (:142) records that the post's text does not print BPS's December rate.
- data/README:50 and :78 still say only that chart 2 shows the BPS-based rate in some years.

The other Traps bullets are unchanged by round 4. Spot checks:
- xlrd reads damodaran_histretSP.xls with datemode 1, the Mac 1904 system.
- The last row of bi_data_inflasi.xlsx is (285, 'Desember 2002', '0,00 %').
- The CPF units mismatch is stated at data/README:98.
- FULL_DESCRIPTION holds embedded line breaks: visible in the file head and counted in round 1.
- The ILO empty responses are recorded at data/README:131 and :147.
- The HTTP 500 event at vet time was not re-tested, as in round 1, and is outside round 4's change. | K: Only Traps line 158 changed: the 4.json to 5.json diff of data/README.md deletes only '; the post shows both'. The other six Traps lines are byte-identical, and data/README.md equals docs/data-README.src.md (diff empty). Line 158 agrees with :50, which says the headline series is BPS's CPI, linked across base years by overlap. That rests on the IMF DSBB quote at msci-fear-chain/docs/provenance-audit.md:304: 'linking reweighted index to historical index is made by the overlap index = 100'. :50 also says the December-to-December change differs from BPS's published December rate for Desember 2008, 2013 and 2020, which fits 'in some window years'. results.json year_by_year imf_bps_gap_pp gives 2008 -0.83, 2013 -0.66 and 2020 -0.095; every other year is under 0.05 in absolute value (2005 is -0.033). make_charts.py:119 draws BPS circles where the gap is at least 0.05, and the opened jh-2-jht-real.png shows circles only at 2008, 2013 and 2020. The chart 2 note says the two measures 'differ in a few years', and :78 says 'in some years'. The deletion also removes a conflict with design A5's last bullet (design.md:142): 'The post's text does not print BPS's December rate or name those years; chart 2 shows the BPS-based rate in some years.' A recursive grep outside verdicts, .rounds and sources finds no surface still saying 'shows both'.
